newsitem.title: UK: BP may reach income target ahead of schedule.
newsitem.headline: BP may reach income target ahead of schedule.

text.p: British Petroleum Co Plc said on Wednesday its target to improve annual income by $1.5 billion a year by the end of the decade could be delivered at least a year ahead of schedule.
BP added that it was confident it could grow production by 5.0 percent a year over the next decade and replace higher output with annual additions of new reserves.
The company also said it could be producing some 2.5 million barrels of oil and gas a day within the next decade, an increase of one million barrels a day on current output.

BP expected to boost daily production to 250,000 barrels in both the Gulf of Mexico and South America and maintain output from its two established provinces, the North Sea and Alaska, at their current levels of about a half a million barrels a day each.

"Add to that new production from the Caspian, from North and West Africa and from Asia, and we can expect a total of around 2.5 million barrels -- two-thirds higher than our current level," chief executive John Browne said in a statement.

He added that BP's capital spend this year would total $5.6 billion, with some $1.5 billion going to projects due to generate income before 2000. Browne said BP expected to continue last year's pace of expansion, aiming at sustainable growth of about 10 percent a year with a debt level of $7.0-$8.0 billion.
In 1996, BP delivered $600 million towards its target of adding $1.5 billion, from a 1995 base, to underlying annual earnings by the turn of the century.

"We now believe we can deliver at least another $300 million of improvement this year, and that puts us well on course to hit our millennium target of an extra annual $1.5 billion at least a year ahead of schedule," Browne said.
